topic.title: The First Time You Translate a Project
topic.shortdesc: What to expect the very first time you run translation in a project.

body.p: The very first time you run a translation job in a project, the agent has nothing to reuse yet, so it creates everything the translated content needs:

ul.li: A translated publication, with a translated copy of every topic and map reachable from the source publication.

body.p: The agent also copies every binary resource referenced from the DITA map (for example images and other non-translatable files used by the publication), and creates the folders required by the project's default structure. See Choosing a Project Structure for Translation for how these folders are laid out.

The agent tries to reproduce, for each target language, the deliverables that already exist for the source language, so the translated publication can be built and published the same way as the original. If you want a different set of deliverables for a target language, instruct the agent accordingly (see Customizing the Translation Behavior).

p.note: Because this first translation sets up the project structure and conventions that later jobs will follow, try it first on a small publication. This lets you check that the agent created the folders, translation index, and deliverables the way you expect before you translate the rest of your content.

body.p: The steps for starting a translation job, following it, and reviewing the result are the same as for any later job. See Following and Managing a Translation Job and the Getting Started with Translation walkthrough.
